```{python}
def mid(name):
    """A parameter name inside a sentence: 'load pH', but 'Equil/Wash-1 conductivity' as it stands."""
    first = name.split()[0]
    keep = "/" in first or "-" in first or first[1:] != first[1:].lower()
    return name if keep else name[0].lower() + name[1:]


N = {k: mid(p.name) for k, p in P.items()}
MV = list(D.rsm_factors(UO))

assert abs(D.to_natural(UO, "load", 0.0) - load_mid) < 1e-9 and load_sp > load_mid
load_unit = P["load"].unit

assert set(iac_here["response"]) == set(R.values())

# the letter codes of the matrices, for their captions
LEGEND = " ".join(f"{LET[k]}, {N[k]}." for k in MV)


def coded(df):
    """A planned matrix as the appendix sets it: run type first and merged, coded levels with signs."""
    d = df.rename(columns={"Type": "Run type"}).copy()
    d["Run type"] = d["Run type"].map({"factorial": "Factorial", "axial": "Axial", "center": "Centre"})
    for c in [LET[k] for k in MV]:
        d[c] = d[c].map(lambda v: "−1" if v < 0 else ("+1" if v > 0 else "0"))
    d["Run"] = d["Run"].astype(int).astype(str)
    return d[["Run type", "Run"] + [LET[k] for k in MV]]
```

# Purpose and scope {#sec-purpose}

This plan sets out the Stage 1 process characterization of the anion exchange chromatography step of the A-Mab drug substance process [@fda2011]. The step is Step `{python} uo.step` of the train and the last chromatography step before virus filtration. It is operated in flow-through mode. The characterization supports the transfer of the process from the development site to the commercial drug substance site under the Process Transfer Plan PTP-001. It is run on a scale-down model of the manufacturing column (@sec-sdm).

The study covers the `{python} W(n_par)` process parameters that the risk assessment RA-001 carried forward for this step. Of these, `{python} W(n_mv)` are studied in a screening design and a response-surface design, and `{python} uv_mid` `{python} uv_verb` assessed one factor at a time. The outputs measured on the pool are host cell protein, the log reduction factors of the two model viruses, fragments and step yield. The commercial process runs at a bioreactor scale of `{python} f"{V['commercial_scale_l']:,}"` L, and the anion exchange step processes the cation exchange pool of one batch at that scale.

Three activities lie outside this plan. Resin packing, sanitization and life cycle are qualified under the resin procedure SOP-2008, and none of them is varied here. Confirmation of the ranges at commercial scale belongs to Stage 2 and is made during process performance qualification (PPQ). The small-virus retentive filter is characterized under its own plan, PCP-009, and this study claims no clearance that belongs to that filter.

## Changes in this revision {#sec-changes}

Version 1.0 of this plan was approved on `{python} v1_date`, before the first study of this step began on `{python} first_start` (the qualification study `{python} first_study`). Version 2.0 replaces it and is issued under the QA investigation INV-001. QA opened INV-001 on `{python} INV["opened"]` after its review of the master report PCMR-001 Version 1.0 for BLA readiness, and closed it on `{python} INV["closed"]`. INV-001 found that the criteria used to judge each step in the proven acceptable range analysis had been set after the data were seen and were in no approved protocol (INV-001 finding 1). The revision history also names INV-002, the investigation of the response-surface models against the adequacy criteria of PCMP-001 Version 2.0. The paired report PCR-008 states what that investigation means for this step.

Version 2.0 keeps the designs, the sampling, the spiking and the decision rules of Version 1.0, except where the master plan PCMP-001 Version 2.0 sets a rule in their place. It makes the following changes.

1. The outputs of the step are judged against the intermediate acceptance criteria that PCMP-001 §7.3 derives a priori from the drug substance criteria and the platform worst cases, with no margin (@sec-par). They replace the limits that Version 1.0 applied (@tbl-criteria-change).
2. Quality attributes are judged on a single batch, through the `{python} pi` % prediction interval. Viral clearance is judged at the worst case within the NOR, on the mean predicted log reduction factor at the least favourable combination of the other parameters (@sec-criteria). Version 1.0 judged every response on a single batch.
3. The scale-down model is qualified for each output by its offset from manufacturing scale, not by a test of equivalence. The qualification runs and the offsets come before the first characterization run, and the decision is made at analysis (@sec-sdm). Version 1.0 accepted the model only where no statistically significant difference between the scales was found, and allowed no characterization run on a model that had not passed.
4. Fragments are a response of both designs and are measured by nrCE-SDS (AMV-3020), following the method decision `{python} AMD["id"]` of `{python} AMD["date"]` (@sec-analytical). Version 1.0 did not measure fragments at this step.
5. Model adequacy is judged on the four conditions of PCMP-001 §7.2, which carry numerical limits, and on two tests that every plan of the campaign applies in the same way, one on the residuals and one on the influence of single runs (@sec-stats). Version 1.0 judged adequacy on the lack of fit test and an inspection of the residuals. It set no limit on the gap between R² and predicted R², and it allowed a model with significant lack of fit to be used where its residual standard error was small against the margin to the limit. That allowance is withdrawn.
6. The platform worst cases of this step on which the criteria of the upstream steps rely are verified in PCR-008, by the rule of PCMP-001 §7.5 (@sec-criteria).
7. The execution window of every study is recorded (@sec-schedule), and the revision history gives the date on which Version 1.0 was approved. The Version 1.0 records gave no execution dates, and the Version 1.0 title block carried `{python} REV1["effective"]`, the date on which the Version 1.0 reports were approved (INV-001 finding 5).
8. Capability is judged against the campaign thresholds of PCMP-001 §7.9, and the integrated model of the train gives the probability that the drug substance is out of specification (@sec-stats).
9. The description of the coded units is corrected. Version 1.0 stated that every set-point is coded 0, which does not hold for protein load, whose set-point lies above the centre of its range (@sec-stats).

@tbl-criteria-change compares the criteria of the two versions. Version 1.0 judged pool host cell protein against `{python} f"{r1_hcp:.1f}"` ng/mg. That limit was the drug substance limit carried back through the nominal clearance of the later steps of this campaign and then divided by a margin of `{python} f"{r1_margin:g}"` (INV-001 finding 2). Version 1.0 judged the two model viruses against step floors, each the cumulative requirement minus the nominal clearance of the other steps of this campaign. These limits were applied at analysis and were in no approved plan (INV-001 finding 1). The host cell protein criterion of Version 2.0 is wider than the Version 1.0 limit, and the two viral clearance criteria are stricter. Fragments carry a criterion at this step for the first time.

# Objectives {#sec-objectives}

The study has the following objectives.

1. Quantify the effect of each multivariate parameter on pool host cell protein, on the log reduction factors of XMuLV and MVM, on fragments and on step yield, over the ranges in @tbl-params.
2. Define the multivariate operating region within which every output with a criterion at this step meets it, and locate the edge of that region.
3. Establish a proven acceptable range for each parameter and each attribute with a criterion, and confirm that the NOR lies inside it.
4. Classify each parameter under the parameter classification procedure SOP-4001, from the effects shown in the study and from how well the parameter can be controlled.
5. Show that the step meets its platform claims for both model viruses at the worst case within the NOR, and justify the Stage 2 ranges and the part of the control strategy that this step carries.
6. Verify the platform worst cases of this step on which the criteria of the upstream steps rely.

The designs of @sec-design serve the first three objectives, and the classification rules of @sec-criteria, applied to their results, serve the fourth. The spiking runs (@sec-sdm and @sec-sampling) and the analysis of @sec-par serve the fifth. The verification rule of @sec-criteria serves the sixth. The paired report PCR-008 reports each objective.

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis {#sec-prior}

## Unit-operation description and prior knowledge {#sec-uo}

Anion exchange chromatography is the last chromatography step of the A-Mab process and is operated in flow-through mode [@amab2009]. The resin carries a quaternary amine ligand with a fixed positive charge. At the load pH the antibody, whose isoelectric point is basic, carries a net positive charge and passes through the bed. Species with a net negative charge at that pH bind to the ligand. These are residual DNA, the acidic part of the host cell protein population, leached Protein A and virus particles, whose surfaces are acidic. Yield in flow-through mode is high, because the product is not retained. Product is lost only if its charge comes close enough to neutral at the load pH for part of it to bind, and the range of load pH is set to avoid that.

Whether an impurity binds depends on its net charge at the load pH and on how far the ionic strength of the buffer shields that charge. At a higher load pH the pH lies above the isoelectric point of more of the host cell proteins, so more of them carry a net negative charge and bind. A higher Equil/Wash-1 conductivity shields the electrostatic interaction and lets weakly bound host cell protein pass with the antibody. The two parameters therefore act on the same binding equilibrium from opposite sides, and an interaction between them is expected. The designs must estimate that interaction free of confounding (@sec-screening).

The conductivity of the load acts by the same shielding, but during loading, when the impurities compete with each other for the ligand. Its range is bounded by the composition of the cation exchange pool that the previous step delivers. Protein load acts through the impurity mass that comes with the antibody. Pool host cell protein is expressed per milligram of antibody, so a higher load raises it only where the bound impurity approaches the capacity of the ligand and starts to break through. Within the range studied the impurity mass is expected to stay well below that capacity. Flow rate sets the residence time in the bed. Binding of the small, highly charged impurities is fast, so only a small effect of flow rate is expected within the range studied.

The step carries a modular viral clearance claim for an enveloped and a non-enveloped model virus [@ichq5a]. Particles of the retrovirus model, XMuLV, present an acidic surface at the load pH and bind the ligand by the same electrostatic interaction as the acidic impurities. The parvovirus model, MVM, has no envelope and is small. Its capsid is also acidic at the load pH, so it binds by the same mechanism. For both viruses, clearance is expected to fall as the load pH drops toward the point at which the particle surface loses its negative charge, and as the conductivity rises [@amab2009]. The XMuLV claim of this step is orthogonal to that of low-pH inactivation, which acts on the viral envelope and not on the surface charge. MVM is not inactivated by low pH, so this step and the virus filter carry the whole claim for it.

Residual DNA is a polyanion at every pH in the range studied and binds the ligand strongly. Its clearance is expected to be large and robust to the operating parameters, and it is monitored rather than modelled (@sec-sampling). Leached Protein A is acidic and binds while the antibody passes, so the step is expected to clear the ligand fragments that the capture step releases. Ligand fragments held in complex by the Fc region of the antibody pass with it unless the complex dissociates. On the platform no step after cation exchange changes the aggregate or the fragment level of the pool (master plan PCMP-001 §7.3). Aggregate is therefore not a response of the designs at this step. Fragments are measured, because the pool of this step carries a criterion for them.

The platform anion exchange step was used to manufacture three earlier licensed antibodies, X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab, and through A-Mab clinical supply [@amab2009]. That experience established the mode of operation, the buffer system and the clearance to expect, including the platform worst cases on which the criteria of the upstream steps rely (@sec-criteria) and the platform claims for both viruses (@sec-par). The separation is by charge and does not depend on the fine structure of the antibody. For this reason the study is expected to confirm and bound behaviour that is already understood. The ranges studied are wider than the NOR (@sec-factors), so that the edge of the operating region falls inside the data.

## Quality attributes in scope {#sec-cqas}

The step sets `{python} W(n_set)` critical quality attribute, the cumulative clearance of MVM, and clears `{python} W(n_cleared)` others (@tbl-cqas). Fragments pass through the step unchanged on the platform and are judged in its pool. Criticality was assigned with Tool #1 of the A-Mab case study, as the product of impact and uncertainty, and attributes of high or very high criticality are called critical [@amab2009; @ichq9]. The two viral clearance attributes carry very high criticality by rule, because a viral contamination would harm the patient directly, whatever their score (master plan PCMP-001 §3).

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(cqa_tab, "Quality attributes set, cleared or passed by the anion exchange step, with their drug "
        "substance criteria.", "tbl-cqas", merge=["Role"],
        header={"Role": "Role of\nthe step", "Acceptance": "Drug substance\ncriterion",
                "Tool #1": "Tool #1\nscore"},
        align=["P{2.2cm}", "P{3.9cm}", "P{2.5cm}", "P{3.0cm}", "c", "r"],
        notes=[("", "Criticality from Tool #1 of the A-Mab case study, the product of impact and "
                    "uncertainty. VL, very low. L, low. M, moderate. H, high. VH, very high. L-M and "
                    "M-H lie between two levels. The viral clearance attributes are very high by rule.")],
        notes_per_row=True, size="footnotesize").show()
```

Clearance of MVM is a viral safety attribute of very high criticality. The register assigns it to this step, although its cumulative requirement is met by the claims of this step and of virus filtration together (PCMP-001 §7.4). XMuLV clearance is shared with low-pH inactivation and virus filtration, and each step adds its own increment to the cumulative claim [@ichq5a]. Host cell protein, residual DNA and leached Protein A are formed upstream and cleared by more than one step. The criteria that apply to the outputs of this step are therefore the intermediate acceptance criteria of @sec-par, not the drug substance criteria of @tbl-cqas. Step yield is a process performance attribute. It is measured on every run and carries no criterion at this step.

## Risk-based prioritization of parameters {#sec-risk}

Each parameter of the step was ranked in the risk assessment RA-001 on its potential impact on a CQA and on its potential to interact with other parameters, and the study type was assigned from the ranking. Parameters ranked high on both counts were assigned to the multivariate designs. Parameters ranked high on impact but low on interaction were assigned to univariate assessment. Parameters held to a platform specification with no credible path to a quality attribute were not studied, and their ranges come from platform knowledge and from the modular claims of the prior products [@amab2009].

For this step `{python} W(n_mv)` parameters were assigned to the designs and `{python} W(n_uv)` to univariate assessment (@tbl-params). The highest ranks went to `{python} N["load_ph"]`, `{python} N["wash1_cond"]` and `{python} N["load_cond"]`, because they act on the same binding equilibrium and their interaction is the route by which impurity breaks through. The designs also include `{python} N["load"]`, because the impurity mass loaded rises with it and the ligand has a finite capacity for the bound species. For `{python} N["flow"]` a univariate assessment was chosen, because binding of the small, highly charged impurities is fast against the residence time at every flow rate in the range.

The load of this step is the cation exchange pool, whose attributes are controlled by the preceding step under the cation exchange plan PCP-007. This study varies the parameters of the anion exchange step and not the quality of its load. The load material is qualified against the release profile of the cation exchange pool before execution (@sec-criteria).

# Materials and methods {#sec-methods}

## Scale-down model and its qualification {#sec-sdm}

The study is run on a scale-down model of the manufacturing anion exchange column, whose qualification follows the scale-down model procedure SOP-1001. The model keeps the bed height, the linear flow velocity, the protein load in grams of antibody per litre of resin, and the equilibration, load, wash and chase volumes in column volumes. Scaling on these quantities keeps the residence time and the impurity mass per unit of ligand equal to those of the manufacturing column, and the binding equilibrium depends on these two. The resin, the buffers and the packing method are those of the manufacturing process.

Qualification compares the model, run at set-point, with batches made at manufacturing scale. The outputs compared are step yield, pool host cell protein, residual DNA, leached Protein A, the pressure across the bed and the shape of the flow-through peak. The qualification study `{python} sdm_id` has `{python} n_sd` scale-down runs at set-point and `{python} n_m` manufacturing-scale batches. Its runs, and the offset estimate of each output, come before the first characterization run of the step (@sec-schedule).

The model is qualified for each output separately, by its offset from manufacturing scale and not by a test of equivalence (master plan PCMP-001 §7.1). The offset of an output is the mean of the scale-down runs at set-point minus the mean of the manufacturing-scale batches. It is reported with its two-sided `{python} ci_pct` % confidence interval, each end of which is a one-sided `{python} ci_one` % confidence bound. Where an output is compared at both scales, every judgement of a scale-down result for that output against a criterion first subtracts its offset, so that ranges and conclusions are stated at manufacturing scale. The model is qualified for an output when the conclusion against its criterion over the NOR is the same with the offset at either end of its interval. That conclusion is whether the output meets its criterion at every combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high of the `{python} W(n_mv)` multivariate parameters. It comes from the response-surface model, so the decision is made at analysis and reported in the paired report PCR-008. A model whose conclusion changes between the two ends of the interval is not used for that output.

Of the outputs compared, only pool host cell protein has a criterion at this step (@sec-par). The qualification decision therefore concerns pool host cell protein alone. The other outputs have their offsets recorded, and no conclusion depends on them.

The qualification does not compare fragments or viral clearance at the two scales, so their offset is unknown, not zero. Both are judged as the model predicts them. For viral clearance the judgement rests on the spiking model described below, which follows the scaling of the characterization model. For fragments it rests on the assumption that the fragment level of the pool does not depend on scale. That assumption rests on the platform, where no step after cation exchange changes the fragment level (PCMP-001 §7.3), so the pool is expected to carry the fragments of its load at either scale.

The viral clearance runs are made on the same scale-down model in a containment laboratory, as a small-scale spiking study [@ichq5a]. The spiking model is qualified separately, because a virus spike changes the load itself. That qualification confirms that the spiked load matches the unspiked load in protein concentration, pH and conductivity, and that the spike volume stays below the fraction at which these properties move. Spiked and unspiked runs are made on matched load material, so that the clearance results and the impurity results describe the same step.

The centre point of each design is run in replicate. The replicates estimate pure error, against which lack of fit is tested (@sec-stats). A replicate is a full, independent run of the step from its own load aliquot, not a repeat measurement of one pool. A repeat injection would estimate the variability of the assay, and lack of fit must be judged against the variability of the process.

## Operation {#sec-operation}

The step will be operated as it is at manufacturing scale, under the operating procedure SOP-2011. The column is equilibrated with the equilibration buffer, loaded with the cation exchange pool adjusted to the target pH and conductivity, and chased with the first wash buffer. The flow-through and the chase are collected as one pool, from the start of the load to the end of the chase. The pool is filtered and held for virus filtration under the hold conditions of the manufacturing process.

Resin, buffers and column packing are controlled to platform specification. Each resin lot is released against its certificate of analysis and is packed and tested under the resin procedure SOP-2008. A packed column is accepted on plate count and peak asymmetry before use. Buffer lots are prepared and released under the site buffer preparation procedure and are used within their assigned expiry. These inputs are controlled for identity and quality, and they are not characterized in this study.

The chromatography system will be operated in the `{python} chr_desc` `{python} CHR`, which is under calibration and change control and whose next calibration is due on `{python} chr_due`. Its calibration status will be verified before the first run and confirmed at the end of the execution period.

## Analytical methods {#sec-analytical}

Each response is measured by a validated method (@tbl-sops). Pool host cell protein is measured by ELISA (AMV-3012) and reported in nanograms per milligram of antibody. Residual DNA is measured by qPCR (AMV-3014) and leached Protein A by ELISA (AMV-3016). The infectivity of XMuLV is measured by TCID50 (AMV-3017) and that of MVM by TCID50 with qPCR confirmation (AMV-3018). The charge variant profile of the load is measured by icIEF (AMV-3013) and compared with the release profile of the cation exchange pool (@sec-criteria).

Fragments are measured by nrCE-SDS (AMV-3020, under the nrCE-SDS procedure SOP-3015). From the method decision `{python} AMD["id"]` of `{python} AMD["date"]`, every study that measures fragments, at every step, uses this method, so that one method spans the train (master plan PCMP-001 §7.8). SEC reads fragments high in samples that still carry host cell protein, because part of the host cell protein elutes in its low molecular weight window (QA investigation INV-001, finding 6). Fragments are judged on nrCE-SDS results only. @tbl-methods-by-study shows the method used for each size variant in the two designs of this step. Aggregate is not a response at this step (@sec-uo).

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.methods_by_study([UO]).show()
```

An effect smaller than the variability of the method that measures it cannot be separated from that variability. The precision of each assay therefore bounds the smallest effect the study can resolve on its response. The variability of the methods enters the residual variance of the fitted models, and these designs do not separate it from the variability of the process. An apparent effect on a log reduction factor that is small against the variability of the infectivity assay will be attributed to the assay and not to the step. The performance characteristics of each method are held in its validation report.

## Sampling plan {#sec-sampling}

Samples are taken from the load and from the flow-through pool of every run. The load sample supports the material qualification of @sec-criteria and gives the input against which clearance is calculated. The pool sample carries the responses.

The screening design has `{python} W(c_scr)` centre-point replicates and the response-surface design has `{python} W(c_rsm)`. Each replicate is a separate run from a separate load aliquot (@sec-sdm). Load and pool samples are retained frozen, so that a response can be tested again if an assay result is invalidated.

In the viral clearance runs the spiked load and the pool are sampled. The log reduction factor is calculated from the total infectivity in the load and in the pool. Cytotoxicity and interference controls are run for each matrix, and the detection limit of the assay is reported with any result that reaches it [@ichq5a].

Residual DNA and leached Protein A are measured on the pool of every run of the response-surface design. They are monitored to confirm the clearance that the mechanism predicts (@sec-uo), and they are not fitted as responses. Where either moves with a parameter, the observation is reported and carried into the risk assessment, and it is not used to set a range. Fragments are measured by nrCE-SDS on the pool of every run of both designs.

## Statistical methods {#sec-stats}

Each multivariate parameter is coded so that the low and the high end of its range studied are −1 and +1 and the centre of the range is 0. Coding puts the parameters on one scale, so that effects estimated in coded units can be compared across parameters with different units. For `{python} centred_mid` the centre of the range is the set-point. For `{python} N["load"]` it is not. Its set-point of `{python} f"{load_sp:g}"` `{python} load_unit` lies above the centre of its range, `{python} f"{load_mid:g}"` `{python} load_unit`, and is coded `{python} f"{load_sp_coded:+.1f}"`. The centre points of both designs therefore run at the centre of the protein load range. Effects are converted back to natural units when a range is reported.

The screening data are fitted by ordinary least squares with every main effect and every two-factor interaction. An effect is twice the coded coefficient, which is the change in the response across the full range studied of the parameter. A term is significant when its p-value is below α = `{python} f"{alpha:g}"` (master plan PCMP-001 §6.2). At that level about one term in `{python} f"{1 / alpha:.0f}"` with no real effect is called significant by chance. The screening model identifies which parameters act on which response. It is not the model from which an operating region or a range is derived.

The response-surface data are fitted with a full quadratic model in the `{python} W(n_mv)` multivariate parameters, on the coded factors. This is the predictive model of the study. The operating region, the proven acceptable ranges and the verification of the platform worst cases are all derived from it, and the paired report PCR-008 reports its coefficients, its analysis of variance and its diagnostics for each response. A quality attribute is judged on a single batch, because its criterion applies to each batch. A response-surface model predicts the mean response, and at the edge of a region drawn on mean predictions a single batch meets its criterion only about half the time if variability is symmetrical. The judgement of a quality attribute therefore uses the `{python} pi` % prediction interval of a single batch and not the mean prediction. Viral clearance is judged at the worst case within the NOR instead (@sec-par).

Each response-surface model is reported with R², adjusted R² and predicted R², computed from the prediction error sum of squares, with the model F-test, and with the test of lack of fit against pure error from the centre points. A model is adequate for prediction when it passes the four conditions of PCMP-001 §7.2:

1. The model F-test is significant at α = `{python} f"{alpha:g}"`.
2. Lack of fit against pure error is not significant at α = `{python} f"{alpha_lof:g}"`.
3. Predicted R² falls short of R² by no more than `{python} f"{gap_lim:.2f}"`. A model that fits its own runs much better than it predicts runs left out of the fit has more terms than the data support.
4. The residuals show no pattern against the predicted values or the run order, and no single run dominates the fit.

Condition 4 is judged by two tests, which every plan of the campaign applies in the same way. The absolute residuals are regressed on the predicted values, and the residuals are regressed on the run order. A slope significant at α = `{python} f"{alpha:g}"` shows, in the first case, a spread that changes with the level of the response and, in the second, a drift over the execution. A run with a Cook's distance above 4/n, where n is the number of runs in the design, is taken to dominate the fit. This cut-off is a common convention that falls as the design grows, and for the `{python} n_rsm` runs of the response-surface design it is `{python} f"{cook:.2f}"`.

A model that fails the lack of fit test or the limit on overfitting is either refitted with a justified change of terms or transformation, or it is not used to set a range (PCMP-001 §7.2). A model that fails any condition is not used for prediction. Where no adequate model results, PCR-008 reports the response against its criterion over the runs of the design, and no range is set from it. A parameter with no significant term in either model is described as having no detectable effect on that response over the range studied, and the range is stated with that conclusion.

Capability at commercial scale is estimated from the integrated model of the train (PCMP-001 §6.5). The model runs `{python} f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"` simulated batches through every step in sequence. Each process parameter of each batch is drawn from a normal distribution centred on its set-point, with a standard deviation equal to the width of its NOR divided by `{python} f"{sd_div:g}"`, and clipped to the range studied. Capability is reported as Cpk against the drug substance criterion. It is one-sided for every attribute of this step, since each has one limit. It is judged in the master report PCMR-001 against the thresholds of PCMP-001 §7.9. A Cpk of at least `{python} f"{CPK_TARGET:g}"` is expected in routine manufacture, and a Cpk below `{python} f"{CPK_MIN:g}"` needs an action in the control strategy. The same simulation gives, for each attribute, the probability that the drug substance is out of specification. The estimate carries no source of commercial variability that the scale-down models do not reproduce, and confirmation at commercial scale belongs to Stage 2 [@fda2011].

# Study design {#sec-design}

## Factors, ranges and study type {#sec-factors}

@tbl-params lists the parameters with their set-points, the range studied, the NOR and the study type that the risk assessment RA-001 assigned. The letter codes are those of the design matrices in the appendices, and the paired report PCR-008 uses them for the model terms.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.frame(pp, "Parameters, ranges and study type for the anion exchange characterization.", "tbl-params",
        merge=["Study type"], align=["P{2.1cm}", "c", "P{4.2cm}", "l", "r", "r", "r"],
        notes=[("", "Code, the letter of the parameter in the design matrices. A parameter studied one "
                    "factor at a time has no code. NOR, normal operating range.")],
        notes_per_row=True).show()
```

The range studied is wider than the NOR at both ends for every parameter. A study confined to the NOR would put the edge of the operating region outside the data, and a proven acceptable range can be claimed only over settings that were run [@amab2009].

The upper end of the `{python} N["load_ph"]` range lies below the pH at which part of the antibody would start to bind and yield would fall, so no loss of product is expected anywhere in the designs. The `{python} P["wash1_cond"].name` is set by buffer preparation and is the more closely controlled of the two conductivities. Its range reflects the spread that buffer preparation and column equilibration can produce. The `{python} N["load_cond"]` is set by the cation exchange pool and its adjustment, so its range reflects what the preceding step delivers. The `{python} N["load"]` range reaches `{python} f"{P['load'].prange[1]:g}"` `{python} load_unit`, because the impurity mass loaded rises with the protein load and a heavy load is where the capacity of the ligand for the bound species would first be approached. At its low end the range extends to `{python} f"{P['load'].prange[0]:g}"` `{python} load_unit`, so the set-point lies above the centre of the range (@sec-stats).

## Screening design {#sec-screening}

The `{python} W(n_mv)` multivariate parameters are studied in a two-level full factorial design of `{python} n_fact` runs with `{python} W(c_scr)` centre points, `{python} n_scr` runs in total (Appendix A). A full factorial in these parameters estimates every main effect and every two-factor interaction free of confounding, which the expected interaction between `{python} N["load_ph"]` and `{python} P["wash1_cond"].name` requires (@sec-uo). The centre points estimate pure error and give a test for curvature. Curvature at the centre shows that a quadratic model is needed. Each run measures pool host cell protein, the log reduction factors of XMuLV and MVM, fragments and step yield.

The runs are made in random order within one resin lot and one load lot. Randomization protects the estimates against drift in the load material, the resin or the assays over the execution period. Where a design cannot be completed within one load lot, the lots should be treated as a block and the block term reported with the effects.

## Response-surface design {#sec-rsm}

The same parameters are studied in a face-centred central composite design of `{python} n_rsm` runs (Appendix B). It adds `{python} W(n_axial)` axial runs at the faces of the cube to the `{python} n_fact` factorial runs and `{python} W(c_rsm)` centre points, and it measures the same responses as the screening design. With the axial runs at the faces every run stays inside the range studied, which an axial distance beyond the faces would not allow.

The quadratic terms are needed because binding switches on over a narrow band of pH, as the net charge of a bound species changes sign near its isoelectric point. Clearance therefore rises more steeply over the part of the `{python} N["load_ph"]` range nearest that point than over the rest of it. A design with two levels per parameter would fit that curve as a straight line and would put the edge of the operating region at the wrong pH.

The response-surface design is run on load material qualified under @sec-criteria. Where it cannot be run on the same load lot as the screening design, the second lot is compared with the first on charge variant profile, host cell protein and protein concentration before the runs begin.

## Univariate assessment {#sec-univariate}

The `{python} N["flow"]` is assessed one factor at a time over the range in @tbl-params, with every other parameter at its set-point. The low, the centre and the high setting of the range are run, and pool host cell protein and step yield are measured on each. A viral clearance run at the high setting is included, because residence time is the route by which flow rate could act on clearance and the high setting gives the shortest residence time in the range.

A univariate assessment cannot resolve an interaction between flow rate and another parameter. The range it supports is bounded by the assumption that the effect of flow rate does not depend on the settings of the other parameters. Binding of the small, highly charged impurities is fast against the residence time at every flow rate in the range, so residence time is not expected to limit clearance. Should the assessment show an effect of flow rate on any response, the parameter will be carried into a multivariate design before its range is claimed. Otherwise the result supports the range of flow rate as a proven acceptable range, and it does not enter the response-surface model.

# Acceptance and decision criteria {#sec-criteria}

This section states the rules by which the study is judged. The paired report PCR-008 reports the executed study against each of them. A criterion that is not met is dispositioned as a deviation and is not revised after the fact.

1. Scale-down model. The qualification runs are made, and the offset of each compared output is estimated, before the first characterization run. The model is qualified for pool host cell protein when the conclusion over the NOR is the same with the offset at either end of its `{python} ci_pct` % confidence interval (@sec-sdm). The decision is made at analysis, and a model not qualified for an output is not used for that output.
2. Load material. Load material is representative where its charge variant profile by icIEF, its host cell protein content, its protein concentration, its pH and its conductivity fall within the release profile of the cation exchange pool. Load material outside that profile does not represent routine operation. A design run on it is invalidated for the definition of the operating region and run again in full on a qualified load. Data from an invalidated execution are retained and may be used to investigate and confirm the cause. They are not used to set a range, a classification or a clearance claim.
3. Model adequacy. A response-surface model is used for prediction only if it passes the four conditions of @sec-stats. A model that fails is treated as @sec-stats states, and a response with no adequate model sets no range.
4. Outputs against their criteria. Each output with a criterion at this step is judged against its intermediate acceptance criterion (@tbl-iac), at manufacturing scale where the output has an offset. Pool host cell protein must meet `{python} CRIT["hcp"]` and fragments `{python} CRIT["lmw"]`, each judged on a single batch through the `{python} pi` % prediction interval. The log reduction factor of XMuLV must meet `{python} CRIT["x"]` and that of MVM `{python} CRIT["m"]`, each judged on the mean prediction at the least favourable combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high of the other parameters (@sec-par). Step yield carries no criterion and is reported as a performance attribute.
5. Operating region. The multivariate operating region is the part of the characterized region in which every output with a criterion meets it at the same time. The NOR of every parameter must fall inside that region. Where it does not, the NOR will be narrowed in the control strategy, and the change will be carried into the master report PCMR-001.
6. Classification. Each parameter is classified under the parameter classification procedure SOP-4001 by the decision logic of the master plan PCMP-001 (§7.7), from the effect shown on a CQA and from how well the parameter is controlled. A parameter that acts on a CQA and has a low risk of leaving its acceptable range, because it is readily controlled and its proven acceptable range is wide against its NOR, is a well-controlled critical process parameter (WC-CPP). A parameter with the same kind of effect and a high risk of leaving its acceptable range is a critical process parameter (CPP). A parameter that acts on process performance but on no quality attribute is a key process parameter (KPP). A parameter with no relevant effect on either is a general process parameter (GPP), and the range studied bounds that class. Neither PCMP-001 nor SOP-4001 sets a numerical threshold for a practically relevant effect or for a wide range. PCR-008 will therefore state, for each parameter, the size of each effect across its proven acceptable range and the margin between that range and the NOR, and will give the reason for each class from them.
7. Verification of the platform worst cases. The criteria of the upstream steps assume that this step clears host cell protein at least `{python} f"{hcp_fold:g}"`-fold and leached Protein A at least `{python} f"{lpa_fold:g}"`-fold, the lowest clearance seen on the platform. The host cell protein criteria of the `{python} hcp_up` pools and the leached Protein A criterion of the `{python} lpa_up` pool are carried back through these values (PCMP-001 §7.3). The host cell protein assumption is checked in PCR-008 on the response-surface model of this step, by the rule of PCMP-001 §7.5. The model is evaluated at every combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high of the multivariate parameters, with the NOR and the set-point as characterized, so that a later change of a NOR does not move a criterion. Where the lowest clearance predicted within the NOR is below the platform value, the one-sided `{python} vb` % prediction bound of a single batch at the least favourable combination replaces the platform value, and the upstream criteria become stricter. Where that bound is above the platform value and the model passes the adequacy conditions of @sec-stats, the bound replaces the platform value, and the upstream criteria become wider. Otherwise the platform value stands. Neither the point prediction nor a confidence bound of the mean ever replaces it. Leached Protein A is monitored and not fitted (@sec-sampling), so its platform value is not checked on a model and stands.
8. Completion. The study is complete when the scale-down model is qualified for pool host cell protein, every planned run is made or dispositioned, every response has an adequate model or a stated reason for the absence of one, the proven acceptable ranges contain the NORs, and both model viruses meet the claims of this step as item 4 judges them.

A change of a criterion by the verification of item 7 is argued by its risk in PCR-008. The report states who bears the risk, the patient or the producer, and whether and where an excursion would be detected. It also states what the downstream steps must then clear, and the probability that the drug substance is out of specification (PCMP-001 §7.5).

# Proven acceptable ranges (planned analysis) {#sec-par}

Each proven acceptable range is judged against the intermediate acceptance criterion of its attribute (@tbl-iac). The master plan PCMP-001 (§7.3) derives these criteria a priori. Each drug substance criterion is carried backward through the train using the worst case that each downstream step showed on the platform (X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab), with no margin. For host cell protein and fragments no step after anion exchange changes the attribute on the platform, so the drug substance criterion applies to the pool of this step. For the two model viruses the step is held to its platform claim, the log reduction that it delivered on the platform. The XMuLV claims of `{python} x_steps` sum to `{python} f"{x_sum:g}"` log10 against a cumulative requirement of `{python} f"{x_req:g}"` log10. The MVM claims of `{python} m_steps` sum to `{python} f"{m_sum:g}"` log10 against `{python} f"{m_req:g}"` log10. A shortfall of this step against its claim therefore cannot be made up by the surplus of another step. No result of the studies under this plan enters the criteria of this step, and no verification at another step has changed them.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.iac_derivation([UO]).show()
```

Two analyses are run for every pair of a multivariate parameter and an attribute with a criterion at this step, and both are reported. The first holds the other parameters at their set-points and evaluates the fitted response-surface model across the parameter's characterization range. The proven acceptable range from this analysis is the contiguous range around the set-point over which the mean prediction meets the criterion.

The second, the NOR-propagated analysis, scans the parameter across `{python} D.PAR_GRID` settings of its range studied. What it compares with the criterion depends on the kind of attribute (PCMP-001 §6.4). For pool host cell protein and fragments it compares the `{python} pi` % prediction interval of a single batch, because each batch must meet the criterion. At each setting `{python} f"{D.PAR_MC_N:,}"` operating points are drawn for the other parameters. Each parameter is drawn from a normal distribution centred on its set-point, with a standard deviation equal to the width of its NOR divided by `{python} f"{sd_div:g}"`, and clipped to the range studied. The draw treats the NOR as ±`{python} f"{sd_div / 2:g}"` standard deviations of the routine variation of each parameter. The interval includes the model residual and the uncertainty of the fitted coefficients, and it runs from the `{python} f"{p_lo:g}"`th to the `{python} f"{p_hi:g}"`th percentile of the simulated batches. For an upper limit the `{python} f"{p_hi:g}"`th percentile must not exceed the limit.

For XMuLV and MVM the NOR-propagated analysis compares the worst case within the NOR. At each setting the other parameters are set to every combination of their NOR low, set-point and NOR high, `{python} n_comb` combinations in all, and the lowest mean predicted log reduction factor must meet the claim. The claim must hold at the worst case, because viral clearance is validated under worst-case conditions.

The NOR-propagated range is the one that supports a claim, and the NORs in the control strategy are set from it. The set-point range is reported beside it. A range is reported only where the acceptable settings form one contiguous interval that contains the set-point. Where they do not, the discontinuity is reported as it stands and no range is claimed for that pair. A range that reaches the edge of the range studied is reported as reaching it, and no claim is made beyond it. Where an output does not meet its criterion even at the set-point, the paired report PCR-008 reports that no proven acceptable range exists for that attribute and states the consequence for the NOR (PCMP-001 §7.6).

A parameter that acts on several attributes has a proven acceptable range for each, and the range carried into the control strategy is their intersection. Each range is reported in the natural units of the parameter, with the criterion it was judged against. For each attribute the report also carries a plot of the response against its governing parameter, with the acceptable region shaded green and the set-point and the NOR marked. The governing parameter is the multivariate parameter with the largest main effect on that attribute in the response-surface model.

Pool host cell protein is judged at manufacturing scale, after its offset is subtracted (@sec-sdm). Fragments and viral clearance have no offset and are judged as predicted. The Monte-Carlo draws use a fixed random seed (@sec-data), so that each range can be reproduced from the same data. The univariate range for `{python} N["flow"]` is derived from the assessment of @sec-univariate and reported beside the multivariate ranges, with the assumption stated there attached to it. Where a proven acceptable range does not contain the whole NOR, the NOR will be narrowed and the criterion will not be relaxed.

# Data management and integrity {#sec-data}

Data generated under this plan are attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original and accurate, and the records are complete, consistent, enduring and available (ALCOA+). Raw data are captured in the chromatography control system, in the laboratory information system and on the analytical instruments that generate them, with audit trails enabled.

Each run carries the identity of the resin lot, the packed column, the load lot, the buffer lots, the instrument and the analyst. Chromatograms and instrument files are kept in their original electronic form. A run that is aborted or that departs from the operating procedure SOP-2011 is recorded with the reason, and the disposition of its data is decided before the analysis begins. The record of each study gives the date of its first and of its last run.

The statistical analysis is run by a script held under version control, and the script, its inputs and its outputs are kept with the study record. The Monte-Carlo analyses use the fixed random seed `{python} D.PAR_SEED`, so that a reported range can be reproduced exactly from the same data. Any change to the analysis after its first run is recorded with its reason.

A second qualified person reviews the data against the raw records before the analysis is run, and the review is documented. Deviations from this plan are recorded and dispositioned in the paired report PCR-008 under the site deviation procedure, each with an impact assessment.

The receiving site reviews the ranges before they are fixed, because a range that the manufacturing equipment cannot hold is of no use in a control strategy. Statistics approves the designs before they are run, since a design that cannot estimate the interaction between `{python} N["load_ph"]` and `{python} P["wash1_cond"].name` cannot be repaired by analysis.

# Deliverables and schedule {#sec-schedule}

The deliverable of this plan is PCR-008, the process characterization report of the anion exchange step. It reports the executed designs, the fitted models and their adequacy, the operating region, the proven acceptable ranges, the class of each parameter, the verification of the platform worst cases, the clearance of both model viruses against the claims of this step and the contribution of the step to the control strategy. PCR-008 rolls up into the master report PCMR-001, which consolidates the cumulative viral clearance claim across the contributing steps.

The study runs in four phases. The qualification runs come first, because the offsets are estimated before the first characterization run. Whether the model is qualified for an output is decided later, at analysis (@sec-sdm). The screening design follows, then the response-surface design, then the univariate assessment. The viral clearance runs may run in parallel with the univariate assessment, because they use a separate laboratory and separate load aliquots.

Version 1.0 committed no calendar dates. This revision records the execution window of each study, from the date of its first run to the date of its last (@tbl-windows), as the master plan PCMP-001 Version 2.0 requires (QA investigation INV-001, finding 5). Version 1.0 of this plan was approved on `{python} v1_date`, before the first window opened. The windows follow one another in the order of the phases, and no two of them overlap.


# Risks and assumptions {#sec-risks}

The scale-down model may not represent the manufacturing column. The offset rule of @sec-sdm addresses this risk for pool host cell protein, and every claim made from the model is bounded by that qualification. Fragments and viral clearance carry no offset, and their judgement rests on the assumptions stated in @sec-sdm. Design spaces are not confirmed at scale at the edges of the ranges, and confirmation at manufacturing scale is a Stage 2 activity.

The load material may not represent the routine cation exchange pool. An extended hold of that pool after neutralization raises its acidic charge variants. That changes the charge distribution of the species this step must bind, and so it can change what the step clears. Load material is qualified before execution against the criteria of @sec-criteria, and a design run on material that is not representative is run again.

The virus spike may perturb the load. The spike volume is bounded, and the spiked load is compared with the unspiked load (@sec-sdm).

Material supply may limit execution. The designs need a large volume of cation exchange pool, and pooling several batches to obtain it would blur the load attributes that the study holds constant. Load lots are therefore scheduled against the runs before execution begins.

The study assumes that platform knowledge from X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab applies to A-Mab at this step, because the separation is by charge and the platform buffer system is unchanged. It assumes that the resin performs within its qualified life cycle over the execution period, under the resin procedure SOP-2008. It also assumes that the parameters not studied are held to platform specification. An excursion in any of them is recorded as a deviation and assessed for impact in the paired report PCR-008.
